# 1. Install and load tidyverse

The following code installs `tidyverse` only when it is not already installed.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("tidyverse", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("tidyverse", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}

library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5
)
```

# 2. Import the dataset

Keep `retail_sales.csv` and this R Markdown file in the same folder.

```{r import-data}
sales_raw <- read_csv("retail_sales.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

glimpse(sales_raw)
```

# 3. Clean the data

```{r clean-data}
sales <- sales_raw |>
  mutate(
    order_date = as.Date(order_date),
    customer_segment = str_squish(customer_segment),
    customer_segment = replace_na(customer_segment, "Unknown"),
    customer_segment = if_else(
      customer_segment == "",
      "Unknown",
      customer_segment
    ),
    discount = replace_na(discount, 0),
    returned = as.integer(returned),
    year = lubridate::year(order_date),
    month = lubridate::floor_date(order_date, unit = "month"),
    profit_margin = if_else(revenue > 0, profit / revenue, 0)
  ) |>
  distinct(order_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(order_date),
    units_sold > 0,
    revenue >= 0,
    cost >= 0
  )

cat("Raw rows:", nrow(sales_raw), "\n")
cat("Clean rows:", nrow(sales), "\n")
cat("Duplicate rows removed:", nrow(sales_raw) - nrow(sales), "\n")
```

# 4. Key performance indicators

```{r kpi-summary}
kpi_summary <- sales |>
  summarise(
    Total_Orders = n_distinct(order_id),
    Total_Revenue = sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Profit = sum(profit, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average_Order_Value = mean(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    Profit_Margin = sum(profit, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    Return_Rate = mean(returned, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Total_Revenue = scales::dollar(Total_Revenue),
    Total_Profit = scales::dollar(Total_Profit),
    Average_Order_Value = scales::dollar(Average_Order_Value),
    Profit_Margin = scales::percent(Profit_Margin, accuracy = 0.1),
    Return_Rate = scales::percent(Return_Rate, accuracy = 0.1)
  )

knitr::kable(kpi_summary, caption = "Retail sales KPI summary")
```

# 5. Monthly revenue and profit

```{r monthly-analysis}
monthly_sales <- sales |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(
    revenue = sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    profit = sum(profit, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(revenue, profit),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "amount"
  )

ggplot(monthly_sales, aes(x = month, y = amount, color = metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("revenue" = "#2878B5", "profit" = "#E07A5F")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Revenue and Profit",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Amount",
    color = "Metric"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 6. Revenue by region

```{r regional-analysis}
regional_sales <- sales |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(
    revenue = sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    profit = sum(profit, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(revenue))

ggplot(
  regional_sales,
  aes(x = reorder(region, revenue), y = revenue, fill = region)
) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  labs(
    title = "Revenue by Region",
    x = "Region",
    y = "Revenue"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 7. Profit by product category

```{r category-analysis}
category_sales <- sales |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarise(
    orders = n_distinct(order_id),
    revenue = sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    profit = sum(profit, na.rm = TRUE),
    profit_margin = profit / revenue,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(profit))

knitr::kable(
  category_sales |>
    mutate(
      revenue = scales::dollar(revenue),
      profit = scales::dollar(profit),
      profit_margin = scales::percent(profit_margin, accuracy = 0.1)
    ),
  caption = "Product category performance"
)

ggplot(
  category_sales,
  aes(x = reorder(category, profit), y = profit, fill = category)
) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  labs(
    title = "Profit by Product Category",
    x = "Category",
    y = "Profit"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 8. Conclusion

```{r conclusion, echo=FALSE}
best_region <- regional_sales |>
  slice_max(revenue, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(region)

best_category <- category_sales |>
  slice_max(profit, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(category)
```

- **`r best_region`** generated the highest total revenue.
- **`r best_category`** generated the highest total profit.
- The business should protect strong regions, review low-performing categories,
  and monitor discount and return rates.
